doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: Billie's age and her parents' hymn playing
summary: Billie says she was born in 1907, that her mother and father played piano and sang hymns in a Baptist choir, and that the children grew up on ragtime.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, you might ask a question every once in a while. He's running a machine. Yeah. Okay, now. We got your name, Billy. Here comes a bad question. How old are you?
I am 50 years of age. 50 years of age. That's right. I made 50. June just passed. Eight.
And what year were you born in?
I see. And so, did anybody in your family play any music around the house?
Yes. I have three sisters living now. They plays piano. Then I have nephews. I have nieces. They all plays piano. And different instruments. See?
What about your brothers?
Never was no brothers.
No brothers whatsoever?
No. Seven girls. Yes.
And what about your mother and daddy? Did they play?
My mother was a piano. And my father was too.
You remember your grandfather and grandmother?
Well, yes. I remember my grandmother and my grandfather.
Did they play?
No, they didn't play.
So the first music that came along was in your mother and father then?
That's right. Mother and father.
Did your grandmother and grandfather sing any songs? Hymns? Anything?
Oh, they was religious people, yeah. They believed in their church. They were religious.
Do you remember anything they sang around the house?
Uh-uh. I don't remember. Not for my grandmother and grandfather. I don't.
Do you have any uncles and aunts that played?
No, I don't have any uncles and aunts that played.
What did your mother and father play?
Piano.
What tunes?
Oh, hymns.
Just hymns is all?
Yeah, church.
Did they sing?
Yeah.
Both of them?
Both of them. My daddy sang in choir. Also my mother.
And what religion was that?
Baptist.
And you remember any of the special numbers that they liked, that favorites that they played a lot?
Yeah, my mother, she liked this number by Shine On Me. That's the number she liked all the time she played. And my father, he liked the number, Bear On My Shepherd. That's what he liked all the time.
How did the words to that go? Do you remember that other one?
I've forgotten it now.
Oh, yeah.
That all of her sister, we came along, we came along ragtime.
Oh, yeah?
We all come in ragtime, all ragtime songs.
